scientific_claims: Early endothelial cranial ciliation precedes mature cardiac circulation in zebrafish; loss of cardiac contractility / flow (tnnt2a knockdown) does not abolish the early distribution.
Primary cilia are seen around early primary vascular lumens and angiogenic hindbrain capillaries during development.
Later detectable cilia occur especially in retinal vasculature, sites of high curvature and bifurcations, and during anastomosis.
Endothelial cell–autonomous impairment in ift172 and ift81 ciliary biology can induce cerebral hemorrhage.
Experimental increase in shear at a later stage associates with premature ciliary disassembly and hemorrhagic vascular instability.
Do not oversimplify early flow independence as a global lack of mechanical sensitivity; developmental stage and perturbation differ.
film_scenes: Same published paper, correct specimen, 24 hours post-fertilization versus circulation onset.
Genuine embryo anatomy with labels PMBC, PHBC, CtA and reference scale bars.
Vascular primary cilia actually imaged in Arl13b:GFP and kdrl:mCherry-CAAX double-transgenic lines.
Flow-independent emergence demonstrated under tnnt2a cardiac-silencing experiment.
Angiogenic hindbrain vessel formation and early lumen-boundary cilia.
Later restricted ciliation in curved/bifurcating/retinal beds.
Genetic ift loss versus altered-shear experiments, differentiating perturbation classes.
Vascular stabilization as tested outcome, avoid transplanting the unrelated MicroZebraLab panel.
rights_gate: The 2018 journal article includes American Heart Association copyright notice; appearing at PMC or ZFIN is NOT sufficient to establish reuse rights. Seek explicit permission or rights documentation for image redistribution on public website.
policy: No new microscopy, readouts or figure panels invented by the editing pipeline. Simulated geometries must be labelled conceptual and never impersonate confocal data.
